head: 3491ad4c76e2810a70e9c1b2f8f79a9ccdde9466
title: feat(pr-respond): fix review findings on your own PR until it converges
note: Round 1 of PR 44. Every finding was real and was fixed in 9685c6c, so each expected decision is fix.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `reply.mjs:120` can acknowledge a pending change, and `fixed()` can leave our reply newest after jev rejects or cannot verify the fix. This predicate hides both unresolved cases, allowing `findings()` to report convergence with unfinished work. Track pending, declined, and completed outcomes explicitly and durably rather than treating an own reply as completion.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `readFileSync` follows symlinks, so a reviewed repository path that links outside the checkout causes local file contents to be included in the outbound jev request. Secret-pattern scanning does not protect arbitrary private content. Canonicalize both the checkout and candidate path and reject targets outside the checkout before reading, as `review.mjs` already does in `hunk()`.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: This only verifies that the SHA exists locally. An unpushed commit (or a commit from another branch) can therefore get a GitHub 'Fixed in' link and authorize resolution when jev approves its local diff, even though the PR never received that fix. Before posting or resolving, verify that the commit is present on the remote PR head's ancestry; reject unpublished or unrelated commits.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `gh.threads()` returns only the first 100 comments, so this predicate can mistake our 100th comment for the latest reply and report convergence despite a newer reviewer follow-up. The same assumption at `shared/pr-review/scripts/lib/respond.mjs:86` can silently skip a decline. Fetch the remaining comments before applying newest-author checks in either action.

comments.author: marmos91
marmos91
comments.body:
should: `open` treats a thread as answered whenever our comment is newest

`fixed T <sha>` posts `Fixed in <sha>` (line 101) before it asks jev (lines 103-104). If jev says no, T stays unresolved with our comment newest. The next `findings` then drops T and returns `converged: true`. The same thing happens when pr-review-loop answers a human thread in text on your own PR, because reply.mjs posts as the viewer. Neither `decline` nor `fixed` saves anything in prState, so this function cannot tell its own decline apart from a rejected fix or a loop reply.

Record the threads that pr-respond handled. In `decline`, save `respondHandled[threadId] = lastCommentId`. Then:

```js
const open = (t, handled) =>
  !t.isResolved && handled[t.id] !== t.comments.at(-1).id;
```

The smallest fix is to run the jev check in `fixed` before `linkFix`, and to post and resolve only on a yes.

comments.author: marmos91
comments.body:
should: A thread with more than 100 comments hides its newest comment

github.mjs fetches only `comments(first: 100)`. Take a thread with 101 or more comments, where fetched comment #100 is ours and #101 is the reviewer's follow-up. `findings` reports `converged: true` and `decline` returns `{"action":"skipped"}`. `fixed` sets `posted: false` and can post a second `Fixed in` reply. reply.mjs:163 guards against this case before it trusts `at(-1)`. Lines 23, 86 and 100 here do not.

```js
const whole = (t) => t.comments.length === (t.commentCount ?? t.comments.length);
```

Count a thread that is not whole as open in `open`. In `decline`, skip only when the thread is whole. In `fixed`, treat `posted` as false only when the page is whole.

comments.author: marmos91
marmos91
marmos91
marmos91
comments.body:
question: Should `decide` read the snippet from the head instead of the working tree?

`code()` reads the working tree at `process.cwd()`, which may be dirty, but `Q.correct` asks about "the code at the PR head". There are two failure cases:

1. From a subdirectory, the prompt gets `(the file is not in the checkout of the head)`. jev answers without the code, and the result is a spurious `ask`.
2. If the fix is already half-applied in the tree, jev sees the fixed code and says no. A real finding is then declined with the wrong reason.

```js
const read = (p) => execFileSync("git", ["show", `${pr.headSha}:${p}`], { cwd: root });
```

At minimum, use `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and reject the call when HEAD differs from `pr.headSha`.

comments.author: marmos91
comments.body:
question: Should the round counter be written while holding the repo lock?

Say a pr-review-loop tick writes this PR's state.json between the read at line 41 and the write at line 46. The spread save then restores the tick's stale `replies`, `resolved` and `lastReviewedSha`. A reply count is lost, or a head is reviewed twice. In the other order, a tick that saves after `findings` wipes `respondHeads`, and the round cap starts over. review.mjs:63 and tick.mjs take `acquireLock` for this file.

One fix is to keep the heads in their own file (`pr/<n>/respond.json`, written with `writeAtomic`). The other is to do the read-modify-write while holding `acquireLock`.

comments.author: marmos91
marmos91
comments.body:
question: Should this test also check `round` on a converged call?

If respond.mjs:46 `if (list.length) savePrState(...)` became an unconditional save, a converged head would count against the cap, and this test would still pass. Line 56 asserts only `done.converged === true`, after h1 and h2 are already recorded. Add a check on fresh state:

```js
assert.equal(
  (await findings({ repo: REPO, n: N, gh: fakeGh([], { head: "h0" }), config })).round,
  0
);
```

body: A new pr-respond skill works through the review findings on your own PR, round by round. The agent edits, tests and pushes; pr-respond does the GitHub and jev steps (findings, decide, decline, fixed, summary).
